summary: Generate new-form food or beverage ideas from zero on the three competition axes, with live novelty checks on the Thai market, then judge and pick finalists

axes.axis_note: Generated fresh from the case brief on 2026-10-18 without using the earlier team candidates, from about 41 Thai and English web searches (most facts come from search snippets, not full texts). Three ideas return none_found (green-banana resistant-starch RTD, jackfruit-seed RTD, cassava-leaf protein RTD, the last with a serious cyanide-safety barrier), and five already exist in Thailand or abroad, so they are benchmarks rather than novel bets. Green-banana RS and seaweed fibre are fibre-led and may overlap in concept with the earlier fibre soda candidate. Thai FDA notifications 445 to 448 (published 4 January 2024, enforced 2 July 2024) govern nutrition labels and health claims, so blood-sugar and heart claims must be dropped, but the exact protein and fibre thresholds were not verified.

axes.axis_note: Six of seven formats already exist somewhere (an edible grain cup sold by a Thai maker, the Ooho membrane abroad, scent-led drinking from air up, sphere ice in bars, dose caps for probiotics, and compressed coffee cubes in the US), so any Thai entry would need its novelty in flavour, ingredient or ritual rather than in the format itself. The one open gap, a leaf-wrapped frozen drink, returned none found after 6 searches, but its food-safety, cold-chain and leaf-supply feasibility are weakly grounded. Retail checks at Makro, Tops, 7-Eleven, Lazada and Shopee were run only through combined queries, and Boots and Villa Market were not searched, so direct store and marketplace checks are still needed. Searches were run on 2026-10-18, and several sources are dated (2013 to 2019). The earlier team candidates (citrus, malt fibre, premium glass, tea, fibre soda) were not used as starting points.

finalists.name: Leaf-wrapped frozen coconut drink pop
finalists.why: Scores N2 F2 Fe1 C1 (total 6). Novelty: six Thai and English searches found no frozen drink or drink sealed in a leaf; the leaf wraps that exist are for produce (Rimping, Chiang Mai, 2019) and for leaf-wrapped food, so the drink format is unverified rather than proven absent. Fit: peel-open-and-sip while it thaws is a new consumption ritual. Feasibility is capped at 1 because a leaf is not waterproof and a thawing coconut liquid needs an inner film, which conflicts with the plastic-free reason to buy; leaf supply and cold-chain costs are also unverified. Consumer: plastic-free buyers are named with a reason, but the evidence is about produce, not drinks.
finalists.kill_test: Kill if a leaf-only wrap (no inner film) leaks during a 2-hour thaw at 30 C, and any inner film needed to stop leaks removes the plastic-free reason to buy.
finalists.first_test_in_3_days: Freeze 30 coconut-milk pops in two wraps (leaf only, and leaf with a food-grade inner film). Thaw 15 of each at 30 C for 2 hours and log leaks. Then run a 20-person blind intercept in a Bangkok office or market: peel-and-sip versus a cup, a willingness-to-pay question, and whether the wrap reads as plastic-free.

finalists.name: Midlife women standardised-isoflavone unsweetened soy drink
finalists.why: Scores N2 F2 Fe1 C1 (total 6). Novelty: four Thai and English product searches found no soy drink with a labelled isoflavone dose; the closest product is a Singapore isoflavone capsule (Holistic Way, Aug 2026), a different format. Fit: targets women aged 40 to 59 with hot flushes and sleep problems, a named group tied to a hormonal-health gap reported by Mintel's Thailand women's wellness report (only the public summary was read; the report is paywalled). Feasibility is capped at 1: no Thai isoflavone extract supplier was verified, the supplement-versus-food registration route and menopause claim wording are unresolved, and dose safety needs warnings. Consumer: named target and reason, but no Thai demand test yet.
finalists.kill_test: Kill if a desk check of Thai FDA food and supplement registration and health-claim notifications, or a registration adviser's answer, shows the pack can carry only nutrient content and no menopause-linked benefit, because that removes the midlife reason to buy.
finalists.first_test_in_3_days: Spike plain soy milk with a standardised isoflavone powder from a public supplier at two dose levels, with the dose range flagged for review. Run a blind taste and purchase-intent test with 30 Thai women aged 40 to 59, and check the powder's certificate of analysis.

finalists.name: Thai-herb non-alcoholic evening RTD for sober-curious adults
finalists.why: Scores N1 F2 Fe2 C1 (total 6). Novelty is provisional: only two product searches were run. Bangkok venues (STOCKHOLME Sober Bar, The Sarojin's alcohol-free menu) and Thai no-alcohol beer exist, but no canned or bottled Thai-botanical non-alcoholic RTD was found, so the verdict is unclear rather than none found. Fit: sober-curious adults are a trend-driven target supported by Thai-market sources (Innova Market Insights, Dec 2025; GlobalData; a Thai Post column citing Mintel 2023 on Gen Z). Feasibility is strong: Thai botanicals and a canning or retort co-packer are public routes. Consumer: named target and reason, but no Thai survey; the NSO 9.6 percent figure is a youth drinking rate and must not be used as a sober-curious rate.
finalists.kill_test: Kill if a store and online audit (Makro, Tops, 7-Eleven, Lazada, Shopee, Boots, Villa Market) finds a Thai-botanical non-alcoholic RTD already sold with an evening or alcohol-alternative position.
finalists.first_test_in_3_days: Run a blind taste of three Thai-botanical bases (for example lemongrass with kaffir lime, butterfly pea with lime, pandan with ginger) with 40 adults aged 22 to 35 who drink little or no alcohol, then ask purchase intent at a 50 to 70 THB price point.

judge.recommendation: Scoring used the brief's four 0-to-2 criteria. Novelty is judged on Thailand only, as the brief states: 2 means no Thai product or close variant was found, 1 means a close variant exists in Thailand in another format or the search was too thin to close the question, 0 means a Thai product of the same concept exists or is licensed. Fit asks whether the idea answers its axis, feasibility asks whether a Thai team can make it with public routes and no unresolved safety barrier, and consumer case asks for a named target with a reason and Thai-market evidence. Nine ideas score 0 on novelty (Wolffia, sacha inchi, cricket, grain cup, textured meal, PM2.5 drink, and others), so they are out regardless of other scores. Three finalists tie at 6 of 8: the leaf-wrapped frozen drink pop, the midlife isoflavone soy drink, and the Thai-herb non-alcoholic evening RTD. Ties were broken by the strength of the novelty evidence and by how testable the barrier is in three days. Axis 1 has no finalist; its best idea is the green-banana RS2 RTD (5), the first reserve. Existing products in the set: Wolffia (Flo), Mister Cone, the sacha inchi licence (Nikao), cricket powder and bites, Mellow Puree, P80, sphere-ice moulds, and the abroad okara, seaweed, air up, Ooho and DRYCAP precedents. Novelty claims that remain unverified: the non-alcoholic RTD (two searches only), the leaf pop and isoflavone drink (absence after six and four searches, with the Mintel summary paywalled), the scent lid (no evidence air up sells in Thailand), the membrane sphere (Thai popping boba not confirmed by search), and the jackfruit and dose-cap ideas (Thai boiled seed snacks and herbal sachets come from judge knowledge). The ideas file marks several items exists on abroad precedent, which the brief's Thailand-only test does not count; the judge applied the brief's rule and flagged the abroad precedents as fast-follower risk. The judge checked three claims live: the Mahidol-Nikao licence is confirmed, while air up and Thai popping boba returned no Thai evidence. The team's docx corpus was not used as a source.
open_questions_for_team: Does the organiser accept abroad-only precedent as novel? The judge applied the brief's Thailand-only rule; if abroad precedent counts, several finalists fall.

Does the team want one idea per axis? If so, swap the isoflavone drink or the non-alcoholic RTD for the green-banana RS2 RTD (score 5), after first testing whether RS2 survives the heat and cold-fill steps.
Is Nikao's sacha-inchi drink on sale, and what does its licence cover? This decides whether the concept is closed to the team.
Does air up sell in Thailand? The scent-lid score depends on it, and the search found no evidence either way.
Are popping-boba alginate spheres sold in Thai bubble-tea shops? This decides whether the membrane sphere is a close variant.
What is the Thai FDA route for a menopause-linked isoflavone claim, and does a supplement registration apply? Desk research is needed before any test.
Can a non-alcoholic product be positioned as an alcohol alternative in Thailand without triggering alcohol-association marketing limits? This needs legal review.
Is the seaweed-fibre drink distinct from the excluded fibre-soda candidate? The team must show it is before it can be counted as fresh.
What is the Thai cyanide limit for cassava-leaf protein, and is there a validated detox route? This is a hard stop for that idea.
Ramadan 2027 start date (about early February 2027) is the judge's own estimate and needs checking if the sahur idea is revisited.
The Mintel women's wellness report is paywalled and only its public summary was read; the isoflavone consumer case depends on it.
